_comment: All your accounts, one place, shared by every engine. This is the minimum global config : everything engine-specific lives in that engine's folder. The channel set is open: add newsletter, threads, reddit, podcast, ... freely; runlog.py --channel is free text and a channel only needs an entry here if you want config for it.
_channel_keys: Optional per-channel keys the scripts honour: primary_metric (overrides the engine's own for runs on this channel) and metric_delay_hours (how long after publish before the number is worth reading : due_metrics.py defaults to 72, right for social; set e.g. 336 for blog/Search Console, 24 for email replies).
_accounts_note: ONE account on a channel: fill in `handle` and ignore `accounts`. SEVERAL (a second language, a founder account beside the brand account, a test account): list them all in `accounts` and let `handle` name the default. No script parses this list : it exists so you and the next agent can answer 'which accounts do we actually have, and what is each one for' without logging into anything. Keep it current; a stale handle here is how a clip gets posted to the wrong account.

_account_shape.handle: @name : exactly as it appears on the platform
_account_shape.url: the profile URL, so it is one click away
_account_shape.purpose: what this account is for : the language, the audience, the brand
_account_shape.posting_id: how your posting tool refers to it when that differs from the handle (a profile name, a channel id). Saves guessing at 7am
_account_shape.notes: anything you would forget: which engine feeds it, when it was started, whether it is rate-limited

_cadence_note: Posting frequency belongs to the ACCOUNT, not the engine : two engines feeding one handle share its ceiling. Four to five posts a day is the ceiling anywhere, most accounts do better well under it, and a burst reads as automation to the platform and the audience alike. engine-video/SKILL.md → 'How often to post'.
_publish_note: Advisory, and an open set : no script enforces it. The contract is: a human approves before anything goes live, and the URL gets recorded. 'api' means the agent may publish directly after approval (sanctioned APIs only, e.g. Bluesky's AT Protocol); map any scheduler you already use onto the same contract.
